scope: A disposable Kubernetes v1.36.1 Kind cluster reconciles native Prometheus Operator Prometheus, ServiceMonitor, and PodMonitor resources. Namespace-scoped discovery RBAC and selector labels limit scraping to two safe synthetic CPU workloads. Prometheus API queries prove no samples before monitor enrollment and exact per-workload stage, measured latency, and quality markers after enrollment. A supplementary check runs the checksum-pinned llama.cpp b9519 CPU server with a tiny pinned model, enables its native Prometheus exporter, and compares a fixed four-token completion with the observed increase in its generation-token counter. This demonstrates one real CPU inference producer-to-Prometheus path in this disposable cluster; it does not prove GPU/DCGM telemetry, native training instrumentation, production attribution, or durable monitoring.

checks.claim: Before monitor enrollment healthy fixture workloads have no scrape targets or samples
The native monitors expose exact training progress, measured timings, and labeled model quality
ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor produce separate scrapes and leave the healthy unselected fixture out
The scraping identity is scoped to discovery in the fixture namespace
Prometheus observes the bounded native llama.cpp generation counter increase
